summary: Our team created an interactive Mars globe to help future astronauts plan their missions safely even in emergency situations. If an astronaut needs to reach the nearest safe station, the globe will immediately cancel the previous route towards initial planned destination and recalculate the best route to the safe place. Our project is important because the Martian surface is extremely challenging. Astronauts have to deal with unpredictable weather, steep slopes, rough ground. By using our project, they can easily plan effective and safe routes.
details: The project works the following way: an astronaut picks a position on a Mars globe, the app draws a safe route to Curiosity (default, white dot) using A* (thermal inertia is included in the path cost) over MOLA topography, avoiding steep slopes. The Alert button re-routes to the nearest safe station (blue dots). Layer buttons: Topography, Thermal inertia, roughness, weather (card), and back (default texture). We developed the app using python, html, and css. Numpy was used for calculations and data processing, Pillow for working with images of maps, pdr for reading planetary data, and pyastar2d for implementing A* algorithm. One of the main benefits of our project is fast and safe route planning across the entire Martian surface, rather than being limited to a specific area without sacrificing accuracy. Finally, our app is creative because we combined real scientific data, interactive map layers, a global view of Mars, and a plan B feature for emergency situations, it strongly relies on NASA numerical data.
